hypotheses: In every session of the project, iaso's band shows in its one line a short count of the loops being worked on (the loops chip), whether or not this session has a loop of its own; the band gains no line. Pressing the chip opens iaso's one docked pane beside the conversation on its loops class, as the command lists them. The class shows one type of loop at a time, with a switch always in view that names the three types, intent, debug and evaluate, marks the one shown and gives how many loops each holds; one key or press moves to another type. Each row gives the loop's goal and progress, live loops first and idle ones apart below. Enter on a row shows that loop's goal, the steps done, what is left and what it waits for. The pane follows the loops while it is open and Esc closes it. A turn's end never waits on reading the loops again: the band reads them just after, its count saying it is updating and keeping the last list until the new one is read. The known problems are the problems class of the same pane, reached from the band's problems chip (SR-410, SR-412); no pane of their own stays. The pane lists no agents or tokens. It acts on a loop in two ways only: reopening an idle loop in a new session (or bringing a live loop's window to the front, SR-414) and sending a message to a working loop, each on the owner's press; it stops, closes and deletes nothing.

given two intent loops, one problem being fixed and one evaluate run are being worked on in the project, when the band draws in any session, then its line holds 'loops 4' and there is no line per loop

given the count shows, when the owner presses it, then a pane opens beside the conversation on the intent loops, one row per loop with its goal and its progress, the idle ones apart below, and a switch reading intent 2, debug 1, evaluate 1 with intent marked
given the loops pane is open, when the owner presses Enter on a row, then it shows that loop's goal, the steps done, what is left and what it waits for
given a session with no loop of its own while another session has an intent loop at plan, when its band draws, then the count shows and its pane lists that loop
given this session has its own intent loop open, when the band draws, then it still grows with the step strip and the task bar as before, and the count stays in its first line
given no loop is open in the project and none is idle, when the band draws, then no count is drawn
given only idle loops remain, when the band draws, then the count names them as idle and still opens the pane
given known problems are open, when the owner presses the problems chip of the band, then iaso's one pane opens on its problems class (SR-412), each problem a row; no pane of its own opens
given the loops pane is open and a loop of another session passes a gate, when the band next refreshes, then the pane shows the new step
given the loops pane shows the intent loops, when the owner moves the switch to debug, then the pane lists the problems being fixed, the switch marks debug, and one more move shows the evaluate runs
given no evaluate run is going, when the owner moves the switch to evaluate, then the switch reads evaluate 0 and the pane says no evaluate run is going

given an intent loop's state changed during the agent's turn, when the turn ends, then the turn ends without waiting for the loops to be read again; within seconds the band's count says updating, keeps the last list meanwhile, and then shows the new state
records.premise:
/iaso:iaso intent I want to improve the way we can track with iaso each debug and intent loop. from any iaso session related to a given project, I want to be able to track each intent loop and their progress, remaining actions, and also show a description of what is supposed to be achieved. Same for the debug loop and the evaluate loop

Question: Today the band shows only this session's own intent loop (step strip + task bar), and pressing the strip opens a pane on that one loop. Where should the list of ALL loops of the project (intent, debug, evaluate, from every session and worktree) be reached from the band?
Options: Count + pane (Recommended) (The band's one line gains a short pressable count of running loops; pressing it opens a docked pane listing every loop, and picking one shows its goal, progress and what is left. The band never grows beyond today's size.); One band line per loop (The band itself grows by one line per running loop, always visible with no press. With 4 or more loops the band gets tall; it changes the 'at most three lines' rule you set for the band.); Inside the existing loop pane (No new band element: the pane that opens from the step strip gains an 'other loops' section. Reachable only while this session has its own intent loop open, or it needs a second way in when none is.)
Answer: Count + pane (Recommended)

Question: This project already holds 10 intent loops on disk, 7 of them opened in October by sessions that are gone (some finished elsewhere, some abandoned). What should the list show for a loop nobody is working on any more?
Options: Show as idle, apart (Recommended) (Loops with a live session come first; loops with no session are kept below, marked 'idle since <date>', so nothing is lost and a new session can still take one over. Nothing is deleted by the list.); Only loops being worked on (The list holds only loops with a live session. Abandoned loops vanish from view (they stay on disk), so the list is short but a forgotten loop is never seen again.); Idle ones, with a way to close (As the first option, and the pane also lets you close an idle loop for good from the list. This makes the list act, not only show.)
Answer: Show as idle, apart (Recommended)

Question: The band already has a 'known problems' pane: each problem iaso is fixing itself, with symptom, cause, fix and state. For tracking the debug loop, what is one row?
Options: One row per problem (Recommended) (Each problem being fixed is a loop row: what is wrong in plain words, where its fix stands (reproduced, fix written, tests, landed, checked live) and what is left. The known problems pane and the loop list show the same thing, so they become one.); One row per debug run (Each time the debug workflow runs is a row: how many problems it took, how many fixed, how many left or handed to you. The known problems pane stays separate as today.); Both levels (A row per debug run that opens onto its problems. Fuller, more to build and to read.)
Answer: One row per problem (Recommended)

Question: How will you see this working? (This becomes the proof recorded on the requirements. The band runs main's code, so a band proof can only be shown after the work lands.)
Options: Command now, band after landing (Recommended) (Before landing: from a second session and from a worktree, one iaso command lists the same loops with goal, progress and what is left. After landing: screenshots of the band and pane in two live sessions, opened on your screen.); Band live only, after landing (Only the live proof counts: two sessions open, a loop opened in one appears in the other's band with its goal, progress and remaining actions; a debug and an evaluate run appear too. Screenshots opened on your screen.); Tests are enough (Acceptance tests for each example; no live screenshots.)
Answer: Command now, band after landing (Recommended)

Question: Should the loop list only show loops, or may it also change anything, such as take a loop over or change iaso's trace?

You said on 2026-11-06: "I want to be able to track each intent loop and their progress, remaining actions, and also show a description of what is supposed to be achieved."
Options: Only show loops and change nothing (Recommended) (The list reads loop state and changes no loop, no trace and no other part of iaso. Recommended: Your words ask only to track and show loops, so a list that changes nothing matches them most closely.); Allow the list to act on loops (The list can take a loop over or change loops from its rows.)
Answer: It would be good if a loop is not being worked on by any session to open automatically a new interactive claude session to work on it and reload context. For ongoing loops, if we could send a message would be nice too

Question: You said a loop that no session is working on should "open automatically a new interactive claude session to work on it". When should that new session open? (Today the project has 7 loops with no session.)
Options: When I pick it in the list (Recommended) (One press on an idle loop's row opens a new interactive session on that loop's branch; it takes the loop over and carries on. Nothing opens unless you press, so the 7 old loops stay quiet until you choose one.); Pick it, plus a notice (As the first option, and the band also tells you once when a loop that was being worked on loses its session, so you can reopen it in one press.); By itself, with no press (As soon as a loop has no session, iaso opens a new session on it unasked. Every abandoned loop gets a session (7 today), each spending tokens until it finishes or waits for you.)
Answer: When I pick it in the list (Recommended)

Question: When a new session opens on an idle loop, what should "reload context" give it?
Options: A brief from iaso (Recommended) (A fresh session that starts from what iaso holds on the loop: its goal, the step it is at, what is done and left, its records, its plan and its branch. Cheap and clean; the old conversation's side details are not carried.); The old conversation (Resume the very conversation of the session that ran the loop, as it was left. Everything said is back, but old loops have very long conversations (slow and costly to reload), and it fails when the old conversation is no longer on disk.); Old conversation, else brief (Resume the old conversation when it is still on disk and recent; otherwise start fresh from iaso's brief. Most complete, two paths to build and keep working.)
Answer: A brief from iaso (Recommended)

Question: For a loop that a session is working on, you said sending a message would be nice. Who writes the message and how does it leave?
Options: Typed in the pane, else by asking (Recommended) (You type the message on the loop's row in the pane when Claude Code allows typing there; you can also tell the agent of any session "tell the card-store loop to ..." and it sends your words as they are. The row shows whether it was delivered.); Only by asking the agent (No typing in the pane: you tell the agent of your current session what to send and to which loop; it passes your words on unchanged.); Leave messaging for later (Build the list and the reopening of idle loops now; sending messages becomes its own later step.)
Answer: Typed in the pane, else by asking (Recommended)

Question: The band has a 'known problems' line today. When you press it, should it keep opening its own known-problems pane as it does now, or should it open the new loops pane at its debug rows?

You said: "Same for the debug loop and the evaluate loop"
Options: Open the loops pane at its debug rows (Recommended) (The known problems line stays where it is, but its press opens the loops pane at the debug rows, where each problem keeps its symptom, cause, fix, state and history. One pane serves both, as you chose for the known problems pane and the loop list. Recommended: You chose to make the known problems pane and the loop list one, so the press should lead into the loops pane.); Keep its own pane as today (The known problems line keeps its separate pane. The loops pane lists the loops without the problem rows, so the two panes stay apart.)
Answer: It should keep its own pane. And the pane that will track each loops should clearly allow to switch from each type of loop, for user friendly loop type switching

Question: The intent is clear and recorded: the loop list and its command, the band count and pane with a switch per type (intent, debug, evaluate), reopening an idle loop in a new session, and sending a message to a working loop. How should the plan and the build run?
Options: Workflow, cheaper agents (Recommended) (I write the plan here, then the build runs in the background as a workflow of about 6 slices (list, debug rows, evaluate rows, band and pane, reopen, message), Sonnet agents, under 10 agents, each slice ending on its tests and its gate shown on the band. Costs a burst of tokens; this session stays free for you.); In this session (I plan and build everything here, slice by slice, with no extra agents. Slower, and this session is busy until it is done.); Plan now, build later (I write and gate the plan, then stop. Nothing is built until you say so.)
Answer: Use the intent loop workflow, classical, with all the expected gates and so on. Using the agents you will judge are worth using

Question: The orchestration session's link sweep has held the machine's one-heavy-job lock for 13 hours and may need several more; this build (slice 5's tests) and another session wait behind it. How do you want to proceed?
Options: Pause that sweep (Recommended) (You tell the orchestration session to stop its sweep after the current link; this build takes the lock, then the sweep resumes. Nothing of yours is lost.); Keep waiting (I wait for the sweep to end, however long; the build and proofs come after it.); Run the tests alongside (I run slice 5's tests and re-pins now, beside the sweep, breaking your one-job rule for this build; both slow down and /tmp may fill again.)
Answer: Yes pause that sweep, why is that so long though?

Question: The last two proofs before landing need you at the screen for about 10 minutes: I make a throwaway idle loop, you type "reopen the test loop" here, and a new Claude Code window opens on it; then I start a second session and send it words you typed here, and you see them arrive, plus a refusal of words you did not type. Each window is a real session that spends some usage. When should we do it?
Options: Now (Recommended) (I set up the throwaway loop and tell you the one line to type; landing follows right after. Recommended because the tests and re-pins are done or nearly, so this is the only thing left before landing, and a reopen or message bug is caught before main.); Later today (I finish the re-pins and the other steps of the done gate, then wait for you; landing waits too.); After landing only (Land on the tests and command proofs; the window proofs are shown once, from the pane, after landing. A reopen or message bug would then reach main and every session.)

Question: A new terminal window should have opened in the throwaway worktree, running Claude Code on the test loop and starting from iaso's brief (it takes the loop over first). What do you see?
Options: Window opened, brief shown (A new window runs Claude Code in iaso-wt/test-loop and its first message is iaso's loop brief; I then send it your words for the message proof.); Window opened, problem (Something is off (no brief, wrong folder, an error); say what in the notes and I fix it before going on.); No window (Nothing opened on your screen; I look at why the launcher failed.)
Answer: Window opened, problem

Question: When you send a message to a loop whose session is sitting idle at its prompt, should iaso start a turn in that session right away so it reads the message, or should the message wait until that session's next turn on its own?

You said on 6 Nov: "For ongoing loops, if we could send a message would be nice too"
Options: Wait for its next turn (Recommended) (The message is marked sent, not read yet, and the session reads it only when it next takes a turn. Iaso never starts a turn by itself, so no tokens are spent to wake a session. Recommended because: You wrote only that sending a message to an ongoing loop would be nice. You did not ask iaso to wake a session, so waiting for its next turn matches your words and spends no tokens you did not ask for.); Start a turn at once (Iaso starts a turn in the waiting session as soon as you send the message, so it reads the message now. This spends tokens each time you send, even if you did not ask the session to act.)
Answer: Wait for its next turn (Recommended)
